text:
olivia_sales: Hey team — prepping the POC for MedBridge. They want a Private deployment inside their AWS account. Main ask: no public egress for model payloads. Need guidance on minimal network handoff (peering vs PrivateLink), subnets, route tables, and what we need for control plane access. POC target: next Tue. Who can own the network checklist?

mike_fieldeng: I can take this. Quick context: if they want our managed control plane but zero internet for runtime traffic, we'll need either VPC peering + route updates or PrivateLink for service endpoints. Also clarify whether logs/metrics can egress. @esme_security can you confirm controls?

esme_security: They require no egress to public internet for inference payloads. Private deployment (our runtime inside their VPC) is best. We'll need: allowed CIDRs, list of ports/ports ranges, KMS access details (if they're using their KMS), and a signed network security attestation.

olivia_sales: Customer provided example CIDR 10.40.0.0/16 and said they can carve subnets. They asked what we need exactly to accept peering and to open access for our inference ENIs.

mike_fieldeng: Minimal design suggestion:
- Two private subnets across 2 AZs for inference nodes (no IGW/NAT for runtime subnets)
- Our VPC peered to customer VPC (we'll provide our VPC ID + CIDR)
- Route table: add route for our VPC CIDR -> peering connection on customer side
- Security groups: allow inbound TLS (443) and a health-check port (10256) from customer CIDR to inference ENIs
- If they prefer PrivateLink: customer creates interface endpoint to our service name (we publish), then they don't need route table changes but must accept endpoint creation per-AZ
I'll paste a short Terraform example for SG + route rule.

mike_fieldeng: ```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "rw_inference_sg" {
  name        = "rw-inference-sg"
  description = "Allow TLS from customer VPC"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [var.customer_cidr]
  }

  ingress {
    from_port   = 10256
    to_port     = 10256
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [var.customer_cidr]
  }
}

resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection_accepter" "accept" {
  vpc_peering_connection_id = var.request_id
}
```

john_devops: FYI on peering caveats: no transitive routing via peering. If the customer uses a TGW, they must attach the peering or use TGW attachments (we don't transit). For PrivateLink: pros = no route table edits, cons = one endpoint per AZ and per-service charges. Choose based on their ops comfort.

olivia_sales: Procurement asked about cost implications for the POC — data transfer between peered VPCs and Dedicated pool costs. Can we give a quick ballpark?

maria_bizops: For a 2-week POC using a small Dedicated pool we normally estimate: Dedicated nodes ~ $600/day (DMing exact breakdown), network: VPC peering intra-region is typically cheaper than internet egress — often negligible for small volumes, PrivateLink charges ~ $0.01/GB + per-hour endpoint fee. Need RPS and avg response size to be precise.

esme_security: Also — we've started the vendor security questionnaire and filled the network section with our baseline controls. Stub uploaded to the handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/handbook/poc/medbridge — please review before we send to the customer.

infra-bot: ticket #POC-612 created for "MedBridge private deployment network handoff" — assignee: mike_fieldeng

mike_fieldeng: Action items from my side: 1) Provide our VPC IDs and CIDR (we'll use 172.31.200.0/24) by EOD 2) Send Terraform templates + SG rules 3) Provide example route table entries and peering acceptance steps 4) Clarify if control plane API keys will be used over the internet or via VPN/PrivateLink — @olivia_sales please confirm what the customer prefers for control plane auth.

olivia_sales: I'll confirm control plane preference in the kickoff tomorrow and add procurement + infra contacts. Thanks everyone — will post kickoff notes and attach customer network diagram when available. :thumbsup:
